ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the center of the figure is a six-membered heteroaromatic ring containing two ring nitrogens, and four substituents can be seen on the ring: upper left is Cl, lower left is Br, upper right is NH2, and lower right is Br. Around the central structure there are also three independent fragments: the left side is labeled ArB, the right side is labeled ZnBn, and the upper left shows an alkenyl fragment connected to Sn. There are also curved arrows and circled step numbers 1, 2, 3 in the figure; according to the question, these arrows and numbers are not part of the molecular structure. Then reason: ArB is transcribed according to the method draft as the phenyl boron fragment [B]c1ccccc1; the alkenyl tin fragment is transcribed as C=C[Sn]; the central diazine/pyrimidine-like core with NH2, Cl, Br, Br substitution is transcribed as Nc1nc(Cl)c(Br)nc1Br; ZnBn represents benzylzinc and is transcribed as [Zn]Cc1ccccc1. The fragments are not connected to each other by covalent bonds, so they are connected with periods to obtain [B]c1ccccc1.C=C[Sn].Nc1nc(Cl)c(Br)nc1Br.[Zn]Cc1ccccc1.

method.method_draft: First inspect the image and explicitly ignore all curved arrows and circled step labels. Transcribe the actual molecular fragments shown: phenylboron from `ArB`, vinylstannane from the alkene attached to Sn, the substituted diazine core bearing NH2/Cl/Br/Br, and benzylzinc from `ZnBn`. Convert each fragment independently into SMILES, then join the disconnected fragments with periods to obtain `[B]c1ccccc1.C=C[Sn].Nc1nc(Cl)c(Br)nc1Br.[Zn]Cc1ccccc1`.
method.CoT_raw: 先描述图像：图中中心是一个含两个环氮的六元杂芳环，环上可见四个取代基：左上为 Cl，左下为 Br，右上为 NH2，右下为 Br。中心结构周围还有三个独立片段：左侧标为 ArB，右侧标为 ZnBn，左上方画出一个烯基连接 Sn 的片段。图中还有弯曲箭头和圈出的步骤编号 1、2、3；按题意这些箭头和编号不作为分子结构的一部分。再推理：ArB 按方法草稿转写为苯基硼片段 [B]c1ccccc1；烯基锡片段转写为 C=C[Sn]；中心二嗪/嘧啶样核心带 NH2、Cl、Br、Br 取代，转写为 Nc1nc(Cl)c(Br)nc1Br；ZnBn 表示苄基锌，转写为 [Zn]Cc1ccccc1。各片段彼此未用共价键连接，因此用句点连接，得到 [B]c1ccccc1.C=C[Sn].Nc1nc(Cl)c(Br)nc1Br.[Zn]Cc1ccccc1。

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: This is the direct image-transcription route: identify every disconnected chemical fragment in the drawing, expand the abbreviations, then write and dot-join their SMILES. It does not rely on reaction inference beyond standard abbreviation expansion.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the diagram as four disconnected species, ignoring the curved arrows and circled numbers: a central aminated chlorodibromo diazine ring, a vinyl/tin fragment at upper left, an ArB fragment at lower left, and a ZnBn fragment at lower right. Note the central ring has two ring nitrogens, an NH2 substituent, one Cl substituent, and two Br substituents.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question instruction that the desired output is a SMILES expression and that arrows in the transition-state-style drawing should be ignored.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use standard chemical drawing-to-SMILES rules: disconnected components are separated by dots; aromatic heterocycles are encoded with lowercase aromatic atoms; Ar in this context is phenyl, Bn is benzyl, ArB becomes phenylboron `[B]c1ccccc1`, ZnBn becomes `[Zn]Cc1ccccc1`, and the vinyl stannyl fragment is `C=C[Sn]`. Convert the substituted diazine core to `Nc1nc(Cl)c(Br)nc1Br` and combine all components.
